Yes—keeping your almond milk/vanilla foundation but changing the *flavor system* can give you “new” recipes while staying aligned with reducing sugar and saving money. Try one of these:

1) **Vanilla-Cinnamon (lower-sugar) creamer**: Start with your almond milk + vanilla extract, then add cinnamon (and optionally a pinch of nutmeg). Use *less* honey than usual, tasting as you go.

2) **Vanilla-Almond or Vanilla-Hazelnut creamer**: Use almond milk + vanilla extract, add a small amount of almond extract *or* hazelnut extract, and include a tiny pinch of salt to balance the flavors (so you can keep sweetener lower).

3) **Vanilla-Cardamom creamer**: Use almond milk + vanilla extract + cardamom (optionally a bit of cinnamon), and reduce honey; if you want even less sugar, consider swapping part/all of the honey for stevia or monk fruit.

If you want a creamier texture without more sweetener, you can also try cashew milk or oat milk in the same recipes.

3) **Acoustic-like fingerpicking test (your “Blackbird” moment):** on the guitar you’re trying, play a fingerpicked passage with a **lighter touch**, try **right-hand technique variations**, and specifically test the **neck pickup**; also pay attention to whether the guitar feels comfortable with the kind of string feel you want (lighter gauges can help).
